In short, the paper proves that language models are not just blindly stacking words; they are navigating a global sequence-level energy landscape. When you look at this through the lens of Karl Friston’s FEP, Chain of Thought is not just text generation—it is a cognitive search strategy. The intermediate tokens are epistemic actions (active inference) that systematically reduce the model’s internal uncertainty (variational free energy), allowing it to explore the probability space and safely converge on the most logically consistent, lowest-energy final answer.

title: The Master Equation of a Messy World
description: hysics progressed by compressing the universe into elegant, predictive equations, anticipating phenomena long before they could be measured. But domains like human language and perception firmly resist such radical simplification. Enter the Transformer: a neural architecture that functions as a new kind of master equation for irreducible complexity. By scaling these massive models, modern AI practitioners have inadvertently reversed the traditional scientific method, empirically discovering emergent capabilities that leave a new generation of theorists racing to reverse-engineer the “laws of physics” governing artificial minds.
